How a mill pond holds the tide

Before 漢かん
よみ字 after the mark.

The pond stores the tide between one turning and the next, and the wheel waits until the head is enough to move the stone. Millers wrote the hours down because the sea does not keep a clock, and a mark on the wall was how they said what the water would do. Families who lived beside the pond learned to read those marks the way other people read a timetable.

The wheel turns for as long as the pond lasts.
